info.title: HEXDailyData API reference
info.description:
Read-only HEX data for apps, scripts and dashboards. Native examples are synthetic; saved-source examples disclose their historical pin. No public deployment or current data claim.

Magnitudes, block numbers and stake IDs are exact decimal strings. Hearts are 10^-8 HEX; raw stakeShares are not T-shares. Use strings/BigInt for integers and exact decimal/rational handling for fractions, never Number/parseFloat. Contract days are zero-based numbers; displayDay = contractDay + 1. Dates and timestamps use UTC. Missing/null is not measured zero. HDS tokens can be signed or use exponents: preserve published text and availability rather than imposing the native decimal grammar.

HTTP 200 does not imply that every component is fresh or available. Inspect status/value/asOf/observedAt, finality, cutoff, reason and coverage independently. Source time, observation time and protocol day differ. PulseChain serving history may contain Ethereum-origin facts before the fork; originChainId identifies provenance. The ethereum enum remains an archived chain selector, not a qualified post-fork eHEX service or a promise of available data. Native examples are synthetic; savedSubgraph examples retain their disclosed historical pin. Neither is a current observation or evidence of deployment.

Cross-field day/chain/ratio/cursor/coverage refinements are also enforced at runtime; addresses normalize to lowercase. No production qualification implied.

x-essentials.exact: Magnitudes, block numbers and stake IDs are exact decimal strings. Hearts are 10^-8 HEX; raw stakeShares are not T-shares. Use strings/BigInt for integers and exact decimal/rational handling for fractions, never Number/parseFloat. Contract days are zero-based numbers; displayDay = contractDay + 1. Dates and timestamps use UTC. Missing/null is not measured zero. HDS tokens can be signed or use exponents: preserve published text and availability rather than imposing the native decimal grammar.
x-essentials.freshness: HTTP 200 does not imply that every component is fresh or available. Inspect status/value/asOf/observedAt, finality, cutoff, reason and coverage independently. Source time, observation time and protocol day differ. PulseChain serving history may contain Ethereum-origin facts before the fork; originChainId identifies provenance. The ethereum enum remains an archived chain selector, not a qualified post-fork eHEX service or a promise of available data. Native examples are synthetic; savedSubgraph examples retain their disclosed historical pin. Neither is a current observation or evidence of deployment.
x-essentials.indexed: Indexed lists use opaque nextCursor, returned unchanged as cursor with the same chain, filters, order and limit. Default limit 50, range 1–100. Null ends pagination. The cursor binds cutoff/revision/ranking identity and expires 60 seconds after the first page. On 409 restart; never splice snapshots or replace a cursor with an offset.
x-essentials.hds: source=hexdailystats selects PulseChain-only source-reported history, not native ledger data. At most 64 records per page; coverage still describes the whole requested range. Pass both continuation.afterSourceDay and continuation.revision with the same date range; both or neither are required. No continuation fields are accepted on the native variant. Null continuation ends paging. Restart a changed revision; do not splice pages or mix reported prices into native/pre-fork series. Source record date does not prove a market-period boundary.
x-essentials.address: Address results separate indexed history and pinned live observations. Inspect outcome, reason, live.page.enumerationComplete and live.expiresAt. A partial page is not a complete wallet inventory. Pass live.page.nextCursor with the same address/chain/limit. The at-block observation expires within 60 seconds; restart on 409. live.offset reports progress but is not a query parameter. Missing indexed/live data does not imply a zero balance.
x-essentials.errors: JSON without Authorization is bounded public browsing, including signed-in sessions. A supplied Bearer API key selects paid mode and never falls back. Stake activity, maturity/principal filters and traversal beyond five global-list pages require paid access. Successful paid 200/HEAD/304 pages count once in the original monthly allowance window; failures do not. Metadata, public requests and CSV are unmetered. Mutating methods are refused; 405 includes Allow. Bounded URL/header/input, process-wide admission and provider safeguards are not customer quotas or an unlimited-access promise. Honor Retry-After on 429; use bounded backoff for retryable 503. Restart incompatible pagination on 409. Errors use error.code/message/retryable and requestId. No arbitrary RPC/SQL passthrough. Cross-origin browser access is not configured by these docs.

Proxy headers do not change identity. These are candidate bounds, not a distributed per-person guarantee. Commercial paid quotas remain unselected.
